records.title: Does codex count as rate-limit-capable in v1?
records.context: vendor.ratelimit-detection is decided: classify only documented signals; anything unclassified stops the slice for the owner (adj show 23). The codex CLI help (codex --help and codex exec --help) documents no rate-limit or quota signal, and the spike forced none. A bad model gave an error item and turn.failed in JSONL (testdata/vendors/codex/04-bad-model.stdout); that is not a rate limit. So a codex rate limit cannot be classified in v1, and automatic fallback from codex is not yet supported by any documented signal.

options.label: stop-for-owner
options.summary: codex stays in fallback chains; a codex rate-limit exit stops the slice for the owner until a real capture is classified
options.tradeoffs: matches the decided rule with no new classifier; a codex limit costs an owner stop

options.label: no-fallback-from-codex
options.summary: codex is never a fallback source; a codex limit stops the slice, and codex may still be a fallback target
options.tradeoffs: narrower than stop-for-owner; still needs the same stop rule

options.label: read-docs-first
options.summary: look up codex's documented rate-limit signal in its online docs before v1, then decide
options.tradeoffs: delays the decision; the spike read only the local CLI help

recommendation.label: stop-for-owner
recommendation.reasoning: It follows the decided rule without a new classifier, and codex stays usable as a fallback target. The read-docs option may still add a documented signal later.

records.title: Narrow v1 for codex, which has no per-tool allowlist?
records.context: launch.permissions is decided as a per-project, per-role tool allowlist (adj show 16). codex exec has no per-tool allowlist. Its help lists only sandbox modes: read-only, workspace-write, danger-full-access (codex exec --help). The S01 spike ran one codex probe with -s read-only (testdata/vendors/codex/03-readonly-sandbox-write.stdout and .repo-status). That run contains only agent_message items and no command item, so the sandbox was not exercised: the model said the filesystem was read-only and no file was created. The spike did not measure whether codex's sandbox blocks a write. grok's per-tool allowlist is also unmeasured. So codex cannot be shown to meet the allowlist rule for write-capable roles.

options.label: read-only-roles
options.summary: codex runs only read-only roles (reviewer, gate, architect); implementers run on claude (grok's allowlist is not yet measured)
options.tradeoffs: keeps the decided allowlist rule for every write-capable role; codex cannot implement or fall back into an implementer role in v1

options.label: workspace-write
options.summary: codex implementers run on workspace-write with no tool allowlist; checks and the read-only fingerprint are the only limit
options.tradeoffs: codex can implement; the per-role allowlist decision (launch.permissions) must be amended for codex

options.label: no-codex-v1
options.summary: codex is out of v1 until it can enforce a per-tool allowlist
options.tradeoffs: narrows v1 to claude and grok; the three-vendor goal waits

recommendation.label: read-only-roles
recommendation.reasoning: It keeps the decided allowlist rule for every write-capable role and uses the one codex control the spike verified (the read-only sandbox).

records.rationale: Owner 2026-10-19: codex runs only read-only roles (reviewer, gate, architect) in v1; implementers stay on claude. The read-only sandbox's write block was not exercised in S01, so the read-only fingerprint is the backstop.

The S01 spike ran codex with -s read-only: a shell write was refused and no file was created (testdata/vendors/codex/03-readonly-sandbox-write.stdout and .repo-status). So codex cannot meet the allowlist rule for write-capable roles.
